assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental and conceptual foundation for how electrons tunnel over long distances through protein matrices, using ruthenium-modified proteins and time-resolved kinetics to test tunnelling-pathway and distance-dependence ideas. This is physical-mechanistic biochemistry of the kind that underlies respiration and photosynthesis, and the principles are general across redox enzymes.
assessment.attribution: A compact two-person credit that fits the three-laureate limit cleanly. Gray is the originator of the protein ET program and Winkler the long-term kinetic collaborator; Marcus theory itself was already recognised in 1992, which eases the priority question.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation across many proteins and by theory groups; the framework is textbook. Recognition is, if anything, late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would view this as a field-defining discovery or as an elegant application of Marcus theory to proteins
Relation to other ET contributors (for example Beratan, Onuchic, Dutton) is not captured by the credited names

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers allowed diffraction-before-destruction structures from microcrystals and, crucially, time-resolved structural movies of reactions in proteins such as photoactive and photosynthetic complexes. It makes dynamic mechanisms visible at atomic resolution, which I value highly.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the conceptual and technical demonstration and Fromme the early photosystem work, while Schlichting is prominent in time-resolved applications; Hajdu (with Neutze) proposed the original idea, and Spence and others contributed key methods, so a three-person split involves real priority questions.
assessment.maturity: The method is established at multiple facilities, but the number of chemically decisive mechanistic results is still growing; timeliness is reasonable, though a few more landmark mechanisms would strengthen the case.
uncertainties: Unresolved allocation between the idea (Hajdu), the demonstration (Chapman, Fromme) and applications (Schlichting)
Credited names exclude some key method contributors such as Spence, so the supplied credit may be incomplete

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is a central physical mechanism in respiratory enzymes, photosynthesis and fuel-forming electrocatalysis. Contributions span concerted PCET concepts, thermochemical bond-weakening frameworks and theory of vibronically nonadiabatic PCET, with direct relevance to biological energy conversion.
assessment.attribution: Nocera (experimental PCET and solar fuels), Mayer (bond dissociation free energy framework, concerted PCET) and Hammes-Schiffer (theory) give a plausible split, but Meyer also has strong priority for early PCET and the line is partly a body of work.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are widely adopted and independently confirmed; molecular electrocatalysis applications remain evolving.
uncertainties: Candidacy rests on a line of work rather than a single sharply attributable discovery
Thomas J. Meyer's early priority makes the three-person selection contestable

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues created a new chemical modality, converting small molecules into inducers of ubiquitin-dependent degradation, with clinical candidates and mechanistic explanation of thalidomide-class drugs through cereblon.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and developed PROTACs, while Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target; Ciulli, Gray and others are also major contributors, so the three-laureate limit forces a difficult choice.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is advancing but not complete; the chemistry is still maturing and recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Approved-drug evidence for PROTACs is still limited
Allocation between PROTACs and molecular glues may call for different laureates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves noncovalent assemblies in the gas phase, giving stoichiometry, subunit architecture and ligand or lipid binding for intact membrane and soluble complexes. It complements structural methods in biochemistry, including respiratory complexes.
assessment.attribution: Robinson has the clearest claim for the membrane-protein and complex work, with Heck and Chait important for methods and applications; Loo and Gross have additional priority claims.
assessment.maturity: Widely used and independently confirmed; the ionisation precedent (Fenn, Tanaka, 2002) lowers novelty somewhat.
uncertainties: Novelty relative to the earlier electrospray prize
Distribution of credit among several strong contributors

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs allows site-specific incorporation of unnatural amino acids in living cells, opening new routes to probe protein mechanism with chemical precision.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the approach in vivo, Wang was a key early contributor, and Chin extended it to higher organisms and multiple codons; Mehl and Yokoyama have secondary claims.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and widely used; a general tool rather than a single mechanistic discovery.
uncertainties: Credit among early contributors may be contested

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single-molecule FRET reveals conformational dynamics and heterogeneity of biomolecules that ensemble methods average away, and has been applied to helicases, ribosomes and transporters, supporting mechanistic models.
assessment.attribution: Ha and Weiss reported early single-molecule FRET on biomolecules in 1996, and Selvin brought distance-ruler and single-molecule motor applications; Zhuang is better known for super-resolution imaging.
assessment.maturity: Established and widely applied, but the 2014 super-resolution prize and other single-molecule recognition reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Overlap with previously recognised single-molecule work
Unclear whether the committee sees this as a chemistry discovery or a technique

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase structures, including the FeMo cofactor with its interstitial carbide, are chemically and biologically fundamental, as the enzyme reduces dinitrogen under ambient conditions. Structure supports mechanistic models of electron and proton delivery.
assessment.attribution: Rees solved the first structures, Einsle resolved the central atom and Dean contributed genetics and biochemistry; Seefeldt and Ribbe are also principal contributors.
assessment.maturity: The catalytic mechanism of N2 reduction is still debated, so recognition for the mechanism may be premature, although the structure is mature.
uncertainties: Attribution spread across five credited names
